papers.title: Comparing Misophonia with Clinical Emotional Dysregulation: A Multi-method Characterization Study
papers.abstract: Background: Misophonia, a condition characterized by intense distress in response to specific everyday sounds, is increasingly recognized as distinct from established auditory and psychiatric disorders. Although it is associated with emotional dysregulation, impairment, distress, and atypical reactivity relative to clinical controls, few studies have directly compared misophonia with a diverse clinical sample exhibiting general difficulties managing emotions. This limits the understanding of its underlying mechanisms and hinders the development of targeted interventions. To address this gap, we conducted a multimethod study comparing adults with moderate-to-severe misophonia and adults with clinically significant emotion dysregulation. Methods: As part of a randomized controlled clinical trial, community-dwelling adults with elevated misophonia distress (n = 30) or clinically significant emotion dysregulation (n = 30) were enrolled in a study to examine sound responsiveness in misophonia. Participants completed a semi-structured clinical interview (SCID-5) and self-report measures assessing misophonia, emotional dysregulation, regulation, emotional processing, psychopathology, and contextual stress at intake. Next, physiological indices of arousal and regulation via skin conductance level (SCL), skin conductance response (SCR), and high-frequency heart rate variability (HF-HRV) were recorded during an Evocative Sound Challenge Task. Results: At baseline, participants with misophonia reported lower emotion dysregulation than the emotion dysregulation group, despite comparable self-report impairment attributable to emotional difficulties. Physiologically, participants with misophonia exhibited higher baseline HF-HRV than the emotion dysregulation group (p = .010). There was no evidence of a baseline difference in SCL (p = .157) or SCR (p = .085). During and after the sound task, groups differed in HF-HRV (ps = .002-.017), with the clinical group exhibiting higher HF-HRV than the misophonia group. No group differences were observed in SCL or SCR during and after the sound task after correcting for baseline (all ps > .08). Conclusion: Findings suggest that experiences of emotion dysregulation are relevant to misophonia but may differ from more generalized difficulties observed in clinically dysregulated populations. Despite endorsing substantial impairment, individuals with misophonia demonstrated lower global emotion dysregulation and greater emotion regulation self-efficacy, while physiological findings revealed distinct patterns of resting and task-related parasympathetic functioning. Collectively, the findings suggest that emotional difficulties in misophonia may be more context-dependent and closely tied to personally salient trigger cues than to generalized deficits in emotion regulation. Conceptualizing misophonia as pervasive emotion dysregulation may therefore conflate clinical impairment with the processes underlying symptom expression and obscure more targeted intervention mechanisms.

papers.title: Genetic, Hormonal, and Psychosocial Factors Underly Sex Differences in Psychotic-Like Experience Trajectories in Adolescence
papers.abstract: Psychotic-like experiences (PLEs) are common during adolescence (prevalence: 17-60%), however, sex differences in the biopsychosocial factors associated with PLEs, particularly pubertal development and sex hormones, and PLE trajectories remains less understood. Here, we leverage data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study to examine genetic, psychosocial, and hormonal correlates of PLE risk and persistence in 7,870 adolescents reporting at least one PLE across BL to Y3 follow-up. Among individuals of European ancestry, higher genetic risk for schizophrenia was positively associated with PLEs. Sex stratified multivariate linear regression analyses revealed sex-specific differences in associations between social factors and the outcome, with parent acceptance (beta= -0.09, p = 2.47x10-02 in males; beta = -0.44, p = 1.5x10-20 in females) and overt aggression (beta = 0.038, p = 1.67x10-02 in males; beta = -0.081, p = 1.53x10-05 in females) showing differing directions and magnitudes of effect in males and females. Pubertal development in males and females and age of menarche are associated with PLE risk, while mediation analyses identified estradiol in females as a mediator of the association between puberty and PLEs in premenarchal females. Lastly, multivariate logistic regression analyses and Analysis of Variance showed that higher exposure to psychosocial risk factors, such as discrimination (OR = 1.47, p = 1.11x10-04) and social victimization (OR = 1.05, p = 2.02x10-02), earlier pubertal development, and earlier age of menarche predict membership to the persistent PLE trajectory. These findings highlight sex-specific social correlates of adolescent PLEs and implicate pubertal timing and hormonal pathways in PLE risk and persistence. Understanding how genetic, social, and biological factors jointly shape PLE trajectories may help inform early identification of psychosis risk.

papers.title: Cannabis Use, Cognition, and Suicide Risk in Adolescents from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study
papers.abstract: Background: Cannabis use has rapidly emerged as a significant factor associated with risk of suicidal ideation or attempts (suicidality) in adolescents and young adults. Although the mechanism underlying this association remains uncertain, cognition is a candidate explanatory pathway. Method: We analyzed longitudinal data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study (N = 10,228; mean age at end of 4-year follow-up 14.17 years, 52.5% male, and 47.5% female). We included three cannabis exposure definitions: one-time experimentation, initiation (more than one-time cannabis use), or ever use. Outcomes included suicidal ideation (SI) and suicide attempt (SA). Mixed-effects regression models quantified associations between cannabis exposures and outcomes adjusting for age, sex, race/ethnicity, household income, and parental education. Additional analyses examined associations of cannabis use with four NIH Toolbox cognitive measures previously linked to suicidality (flanker, working memory, picture vocabulary, and picture sequence memory), and associations of these cognitive measures with SI and SA. Results: Cannabis use was associated with increased odds of SI (ever use odds ratio (OR)=3.18, 95% confidence interval (95%CI) =2.52-4.00) and SA (OR=4.86, 95%CI=3.36-7.03), associations were overall similar across all exposure definitions (all p < 0.001). Cannabis use was also associated with lower performance across multiple cognitive domains ({beta} = -0.08 to -0.16, all p < 0.05). Better cognitive performance, specifically in episodic memory, was associated with lower suicidality: SI (OR = 0.91, 95%CI=0.86-0.95) and SA (OR = 0.88, 95%CI=0.80- 0.97). Conclusion: These findings support cognition as a potential mechanism linking cannabis use to adolescent suicide risk and warrant longitudinal investigation.

papers.title: Plasma Alzheimer''s assays agree on level but much less on individual rates of change
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Serial plasma testing is proposed for monitoring Alzheimer's disease and for trials, but its reliability for a person's rate of change is unknown. METHODS: In 393 ADNI participants with three plasma samples over a median 5.0 years, 15 measures of five biomarkers were assayed on aliquots of the same samples, separating shared change from assay-specific variation at each sampling occasion. Results were tested in 1,093 A4/LEARN participants. RESULTS: Assays agreed well on cross-sectional levels (intraclass correlation 0.75--0.95 for pTau217, pTau181, GFAP, NfL) but less on individual rates of change (0.44, 95% CI 0.37--0.50, for pTau217). Assay-specific slope variance was approximately zero, so disagreement was predominantly random. Three-sample single-assay slope reliability was at most 0.40 (0.34--0.46) for pTau217, 0.42 (0.33--0.51) for pTau181, 0.47 (0.37--0.60) for GFAP, 0.52 (0.40--0.64) for NfL, and 0.10 (0.03--0.20) for A{beta}42/40. Two pTau217 measurements had to differ by 65%--131%, depending on the assay, to exceed measurement noise. Detecting 25% slowing of pTau217 change required 924 (598--1,468) to 4,030 (2,091--9,256) participants per arm, or 532 (357--778) to 965 (655--1,431) with averaged measures. In A4/LEARN, single-assay pTau217 reliability was 0.54 (0.46--0.61), and a 7.3- rather than 4.8-year span raised it by 0.10 (0.00-0.22); a fourth sample within it added little. DISCUSSION: With three single-assay samples, much of an individual's measured change is noise. Longer spans, endpoint replication, and assay choice, rather than additional intermediate samples, are needed for reliable serial testing and trials.

papers.title: The genetic architecture of wisdom and its relationship with health, personality, and cognition
papers.abstract: Wisdom is a personality trait composed of self-reflection, pro-social behaviors, emotional regulation, acceptance of divergent perspectives, decisiveness, social advising, and spirituality. Greater levels of wisdom are linked to better overall health, well-being, happiness, life satisfaction, and resilience. However, the underlying genetic architecture of wisdom remains unexplored. We assessed wisdom using responses to the SD-WISE-7 in 153,384 23andMe research-consented participants and conducted a multi-ancestry GWAS. We identified one genome-wide significant locus (rs2325631, p=1.41E-08) near MANEA on chromosome 6. Wisdom was heritable (h2SNP=0.03{+/-}4.50E-03) and genetically correlated with numerous traits, including greater subjective well-being, openness, and risk tolerance, and lower neuroticism and loneliness. Crucially, wisdom was genetically distinct from intelligence and the cognitive component of educational attainment. Wisdom polygenic scores were associated with psychosocial outcomes, but not cognitive performance in All of Us. This study advances our understanding of wisdom as a heritable trait that could guide interventions to improve human health.

papers.title: Bipolar Disorder and Education: Deciphering a Complex Relationship using Genetic and Sibling Differences in a Multi-cohort Study
papers.abstract: Background. While bipolar disorder has a positive genetic correlation (r~0.3) with educational attainment (EA), individuals with bipolar disorder diagnoses have lower EA in adulthood. To clarify this paradox, we hypothesise that bipolar disorder and educational outcomes share a positive genetic association, reflected in high academic performance earlier in life, but that emerging bipolar disorder symptoms disrupt academic trajectories, leading to the observed poor long-term educational outcomes. Methods. We employed a sibling comparison design across four population-based cohorts (Ntotal = 1,145,795 siblings). First, we tested the association between bipolar disorder polygenic scores (PGS) and educational outcomes (EA and academic performance) in the Norwegian Mother, Father and Child Cohort Study (MoBa) and UK Biobank (UKB). Second, we examined associations between academic performance at ages 10, 12, 13, and 14 and subsequent bipolar disorder diagnosis using registry data from Statistics Netherlands and Statistics Norway (with the Norwegian Control and Payment of Health Reimbursements Databases). Findings. Siblings with higher bipolar disorder PGS had significantly higher EA ({beta}W = 0.03, 95% CI [0.01, 0.05], N=16,746) as well as higher academic performance at age 10 (0.03 [0.01, 0.05], N=17,677) in MoBa. Secondly, individuals with bipolar disorder had better overall academic performance than their unaffected sibling at ages 10 (HRW = 1.12 [1.02, 1.22], N=343,898) and 12 (1.59 [1.16, 2.19], N=619,796). However, individuals with bipolar disorder experienced a decline in academic performance at ages 13 (0.84 [0.73, 0.96], N=320,342) and 14 (0.72 [0.61, 0.85], N=299,039). Interpretation. Bipolar disorder shares a positive genetic association with educational outcomes, reflected in early academic advantage. This is followed by an academic decline in mid-adolescence, highlighting the period of educational disruption associated with bipolar disorder. Funding. The Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Sciences, European Research Council, the Research Council of Norway, the Swedish Research Council

papers.title: Facial Emotion Processing and GABAergic Modulation in Individuals at Clinical High-Risk for Psychosis
papers.abstract: Deficits in social cognition, including facial emotion recognition (FER), are present in individuals at clinical high-risk for psychosis (CHR-P). Altered GABAergic and glutamatergic signalling within corticolimbic circuitry has been proposed to underlie FER deficits in psychosis. We investigated FER performance and brain activation in CHR-P individuals, and whether pharmacological enhancement of GABAergic signalling with diazepam modulates these processes. In Study 1, 24 antipsychotic-naive CHR-P individuals and 24 healthy controls underwent fMRI while performing the Penn Emotion Recognition Task. In Study 2, 24 antipsychotic-naive CHR-P individuals participated in a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover study of 5mg diazepam versus placebo. Threat-related FER performance and neural activation were compared between groups and drug conditions. In Study 1, CHR-P individuals showed longer reaction times across emotions (n=22 vs n=23, p=0.01) and greater amygdala (pFWE=0.01) and hippocampal (pFWE=0.04) activation for neutral>fixation. Lower amygdala activation for threat>neutral (pFWE=0.03) and non-threat>neutral (pFWE=0.01), and lower hippocampal activation for non-threat>neutral (pFWE=0.04) may reflect this elevated response to neutral faces. Follow-up analyses showed lower insula (pFWE=0.01) and medial prefrontal cortex activation (pFWE=0.02) for threat>fixation. In Study 2, no significant drug effect on sensitivity was observed in the full sample (n=23), although secondary reduced-sample analyses, excluding one participant identified as influential, suggested improved overall sensitivity under diazepam (n=22; p=0.0499). After adjusting for global cerebral blood flow, diazepam reduced midcingulate cortex activation during neutral>fixation (pFWE=0.04). These findings highlight altered neural processing of neutral expressions in individuals at CHR-P, and suggest that aspects of emotion processing may be sensitive to GABAergic modulation.

papers.title: Genetic architecture of social anxiety disorder: examining moderation by rural-urban residential environment
papers.abstract: Social anxiety disorder (SAD) is a common psychiatric condition characterized by a consistent fear of social evaluation. Despite heritability estimates of up to 69%, genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of SAD remain limited relative to other psychiatric disorders. Furthermore, the contribution of environmental factors, particularly rural versus urban residence, to SAD risk is poorly characterized. Using the All of Us dataset (N=414,830, Ncases=10,918), our aims were to: (1) identify genetic risk loci for SAD through within-ancestry GWAS (N=1,467-222,500), cross-ancestry meta-analysis, and a European-ancestry meta-analysis (N =788,384); (2) further characterize the genetic architecture of SAD through polygenic risk score (PRS), phenome-wide association (PheWAS), laboratory-wide association (LabWAS), and genetic correlation; and (3) stratify all analyses by rural and urban environment. Across all ancestries examined, rural residence was associated with increased odds of SAD (OR=1.42, 95%; CI [1.36-1.50]; p<5x10). Although no genome-wide significant loci were identified, several loci reached suggestive significance, notably an intronic variant in NEGR1 (rs12065683), a gene with prior associations to anxiety and neurodevelopmental disorders. PheWAS analyses identified ear disorders as the most nominally significant phenotype (p=3.76x10; OR=1.45) and significant associations with lymphocyte count were identified in the LabWAS (p=1.80x10-). These findings provide further insight into the genetic architecture of SAD and suggest that residential environment may modify risk. Larger-scale genetic studies will be required to validate the observed suggestive loci and gene x environment interaction models to form conclusions regarding the true effect of residence.

papers.title: TALQ: A reproducible language model questionnaire for dense measurement of depressive and anxious states
papers.abstract: Depression and anxiety are often assessed weeks or months apart with brief questionnaires covering few symptoms, leaving changes between assessments unobserved. Here, we introduce TALQ, a scoring system in which a large language model rates 52 symptoms from text, and use it to score 491 members of two online mental health communities every two weeks for a year. Ratings were stable across samples, predicted human annotations of interpersonal risk factors, low self-esteem and depression severity, and agreed with inventories completed by the same model. The scores mapped into 12 replicable symptom factors, including fearful preoccupation and social strain. Sleep disturbance and self-harm content consistently preceded overwhelm and emotional pain, respectively, two weeks later. People differed mainly in the states they occupied rather than transitions between them, and 13% entered in a crisis that remitted over months. Overall, our findings suggest that TALQ can measure expressed mental states densely and quantify longitudinal dynamics.

papers.title: Privilege Is Not Enough: Evaluating Generalized Distillation for Normative Brain Age Modeling in Depression, Anxiety and Alcohol Use Disorder
papers.abstract: Models trained on rich multimodal data may depend on modalities unavailable at deployment. In generalized distillation, a teacher trained on such privileged data guides a student using only deployable features. We ask whether students inherit clinically meaningful properties beyond predictions in brain-age modeling, where brain-age gaps index deviations from normative aging and brain health. In simulations, distillation recovered a gap-severity association which an age-trained baseline missed. In UK Biobank analyses of depression, anxiety, and alcohol use disorder, students using structural MRI, functional MRI or biosocial data produced gaps closer to their teachers than matched baselines in 10 of 12 comparisons. Where teachers most exceeded baselines (anxiety in biosocial, alcohol use in functional MRI students), gap-severity associations rose toward their teachers. Our findings characterize conditions for successful distillation, i.e. clinical signal the teacher holds, the baseline misses and deployable features contain, and demonstrate their relevance in a real-life psychiatry application.

papers.title: Bivariate Multiscale Sample Entropy of Frontoparietal-Subgenual ACC Dynamics in Depression During Accelerated TMS at 7 T
papers.abstract: ObjectiveTo examine whether longitudinal changes in frontoparietal (FP)-subgenual anterior cingulate cortex (sgACC) joint temporal complexity differ between sgACC hemispheres in patients undergoing accelerated TMS (aTMS) and untreated healthy controls. MethodsTwenty-four patients with current depressive episodes and fifteen healthy controls underwent 7T resting-state fMRI at baseline and follow-up. Patients received aTMS localized to the left DLPFC using Beam-F3. The same bilateral FP time series was paired separately with left and right sgACC time series. Bivariate multiscale sample entropy (bMSE) across scale factors a1-a10 was summarized by trapezoidal integration as a complexity index (bMSE-CI). The primary test was the Group x Time x sgACC Hemisphere interaction in a mixed repeated- measures ANOVA. Scale-specific interactions and clinical Spearman correlations were evaluated with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction. Change scores were follow-up minus baseline. ResultsThe bMSE-CI Group x Time x Hemisphere interaction was significant (F(1,37) = 6.043, p = 0.0188, partial {superscript 2} = 0.140). Mean left/right bMSE-CI changes were -0.286/+0.124 in patients and +0.323/+0.112 in controls. Of ten scale-specific three-way interactions, only a2 survived FDR correction (q = 0.0435). No baseline or change-score bMSE-MADRS association survived the specified FDR corrections. A random-intercept-only mixed-model sensitivity analysis did not reach statistical significance for the three-way interaction (p = 0.0718). ConclusionFP-sgACC joint temporal complexity showed hemisphere-dependent longitudinal differences between patients undergoing aTMS and healthy controls. These exploratory findings motivate further evaluation of bMSE as a candidate measure of longitudinal neural change in depression. Independent replication, more precise reliability estimates, and prospective validation of clinical relevance are needed.

papers.title: Automatic classification of seizure adequacy in electroconvulsive therapy: A proof-of-concept study
papers.abstract: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is the most effective treatment of a range of severe mental disorders and is annually given to more than a million patients worldwide. Dosing of the electrical charge is critical for efficacy and side-effect burden; however, it is currently based on manual assessment of seizure quality and exhibits substantial clinical heterogeneity. Here, we collected 1,000 ECT session electroencephalograms (EEG) from 130 individual ECT patients and made an expert-level classification of the EEGs into actionable seizure quality categories (null-response [0], threshold [T], and adequate [A]). We then trained a range of machine learning algorithms on the raw EEG data to classify the EEGs into these categories and tested for classification accuracy. The highest performing algorithm was able to classify the seizures with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curves of >0.9 for both the 0 vs. T and the T vs. A categories corresponding to excellent discrimination. In contrast, the accuracy of predicting seizure quality in subsequent treatments was only moderate. The addition of clinical variables to the models, such as demographics, anesthesia and anticonvulsant exposure, did not improve model performance. These results provide proof-of-concept of machine learning classification of seizure adequacy in ECT based on raw EEG data. The findings could pave the way for the development of more objective and personalized decision-support tools in ECT.

papers.title: Community Care of Eating Disorders: Comparison of Online and In-Person Treatment. A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
papers.abstract: ObjectiveEating disorders are serious conditions which sometimes require intensive treatment and are undertreated worldwide. Care can be provided in the community in different treatment delivery modes that could increase access to evidence-based treatment and avoid the negative impacts of delayed interventions. This systematic review and meta-analysis investigated the comparative effectiveness of adult eating disorder community care delivered via in-person, online and mixed (blended/hybrid) modes to provide a global perspective and recommendations for the use of telemedicine in the field. MethodThe databases MEDLINE, Embase, PsychINFO, Emcare, Scopus and Web of Science were searched on 22nd June 2025. Inclusion criteria specified quasi-experimental studies which compared two or more treatment delivery modes. The Joanna Briggs Institute risk of bias tool for quasi-experimental studies was used for quality assessments. Qualitative synthesis and meta-analyses were conducted. ResultsThe daycare/intensive outpatient programme studies showed non-inferiority of in-person and online treatment programmes: EDE-Q Global score (-0.00 [95% CI: -0.23, 0.22]); anxiety (GAD-7/OASIS) (-0.05 [95% CI: -0.31, 0.20]); BMI (0.06 [95% CI: -0.20, 0.33]); and depression (BDI-2/PHQ-9/CES-D) (0.07 [95% CI: -0.31, 0.44]). The outpatient studies showed non-significant differences between in-person and online treatment programmes: anxiety (GAD-7/PROMIS) (0.28 [95% CI: -0.48, 1.04]); depression (PHQ-9/PROMIS) (0.58 [95% CI: -0.59, 1.75]); and EDE-Q Global score (0.73 [95% CI: - 0.91, 2.36]). For all measures, better outcomes were indicated for online care. DiscussionComparisons with mixed treatment delivery mode are lacking, but findings provide credence to the viability of online care as being on par or even better under certain conditions than in-person care. SummaryO_LIDaycare/intensive outpatient programmes for adults were non-inferior delivered in-person or online for BMI, eating disorder, depression, and anxiety symptoms. C_LIO_LIOutpatient programmes for adults showed non-significant differences delivered in-person or online for eating disorder, depression, and anxiety symptoms. But findings suggest a possible superiority of online treatment. C_LIO_LIResearch on community care delivered in mixed mode is sparse. C_LIO_LIThe evidence base is very small, particularly for the outpatient studies indicating the need for more high-quality quasi-experimental studies and ideally well designed randomised controlled trials. C_LI

papers.title: How Does Psilocybin Affect Daily Life Experience and Behavior? Protocol For a Multimethod Ambulatory Assessment Study Within a Clinical Trial of Psilocybin for Depression
papers.abstract: IntroductionAlthough psilocybin has shown promise for treating depression, responses vary considerably, with some individuals experiencing limiting improvement and even adverse effects. Research has largely relied on assessments conducted at discrete time points, providing limited insight into how post-psilocybin change unfolds in everyday life. The Dial-In study aims to characterize daily-life processes associated with differential responses to psilocybin, including factors associated with improvement or worsening following challenging dosing experiences. Methods and AnalysisDial-In is a prospective, observational, multi-method longitudinal study embedded within a clinical trial administering 25 mg of psilocybin to up to 141 adults with major depressive disorder. Ambulatory assessments combine ecological momentary assessment (EMA) and voice diaries for 14 days pre- and post-dosing, and passive audio sampling via the Electronically Activated Recorder (EAR) for three four-day periods to characterize everyday affect, behavior, reflections, and social interactions. Outcomes include depressive symptoms, psychological well-being, and psychedelic-related adverse effects assessed through eight weeks post-dose. Analyses will examine whether affective sudden gains and losses, social support, interpersonal conflict, conversational focus, reflection and rigidity predict differential outcomes. Additional analyses will test whether these factors moderate associations between challenging dosing experiences and clinical outcomes. Ethics and DisseminationThe project was approved by WCG Institutional Review Board, with Emory University relying on WCG as the reviewing board. All participants provide written informed consent. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and scientific presentations. Trial RegistrationClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06512194 (parent trial), OSF (https://osf.io/nx5ky/overview) Article SummaryStrengths and Limitations of this Study O_LIStrength: Measurement of observed behavior, beyond self-report. C_LIO_LIStrength: The integration of ecological momentary assessment, open-ended voice diaries, and naturalistic behavioral observations provides complementary perspectives on post-acute change. C_LIO_LIStrength: The prospective, longitudinal design enables the examination of within-person affective and behavioral changes surrounding psilocybin administration, including sudden gains and losses that may be obscured by discrete time-point assessments. C_LIO_LIStrength: By examining depressive symptoms, psychological well-being, and adverse effects, the study captures multiple dimensions of treatment response. C_LIO_LILimitation: The observational design precludes causal inference regarding the direction of relationships between everyday processes and clinical outcomes. C_LI

papers.title: Investigating Indirect Genetic Effects on Neurodevelopmental Traits Across Development and Reporters: Triangulating Twin-comparison and Trio-PGS Approaches
papers.abstract: Polygenic associations with neurodevelopmental traits may reflect both direct and indirect genetic effects. However, evidence separating these effects is limited and mixed, and rarely spans development or reporters, or triangulates across methods. We triangulated twin-comparison and trio-based analyses in the Twins Early Development Study, using eight polygenic scores (PGS) and repeated parent, teacher and self-reports of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) traits from ages 4 to 26. Analyses included up to 7,259 offspring with observed or imputed parental genetic data. Both approaches consistently supported direct genetic effects of ADHD and ASD PGS on corresponding traits, whereas evidence for within-trait indirect effects was limited. Cross-trait indirect effects emerged for several PGS, particularly in parent reports, and some were unexpectedly negative. These findings suggest that within-trait polygenic prediction of ADHD and ASD traits mainly reflects direct rather than indirect genetic effects, whereas cross-trait associations reflect some indirect genetic effects.

papers.title: Mapping disordered eating symptoms in the ABCD Study through the Eating Disorder Symptom Index
papers.abstract: Eating disorders (EDs) are serious psychiatric conditions that typically onset during adolescence and are often marked by a chronic and severe illness course. Capturing ED symptoms as they emerge is critical for charting risk markers and associated outcomes to inform early intervention and treatment efforts. The Adolescent Brain Cognitive DevelopmentSM (ABCD(R)) Study is one such key study that could accelerate these efforts, but has been limited to date by a lack of clear, clinically informed definitions capturing youth at risk for ED-related concerns. The current manuscript aims to address this gap by defining ED symptom indices (EDSI) with a reproducible framework developed in collaboration with ED researchers and clinicians to identify youth with patterns of ED symptoms and behaviors that approximate subthreshold and diagnostic-like presentations. We describe item-level definitions and decision rules used to construct the EDSI, which include symptom indices of anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, binge eating disorder, and other specified feeding or eating disorders. We then compare youth meeting EDSI criteria with those identified by existing ED categorical definitions in ABCD Study data releases. By providing transparent definitions and analytical tools for identifying youth with potentially clinically meaningful ED behaviors, the EDSI framework aims to facilitate more reproducible and interpretable research related to EDs using the ABCD Study dataset, while also providing a structure to examine the emergence, persistence, and change of ED-like symptoms longitudinally across adolescence and into young adulthood in future research.

papers.title: Persistent or recurrent depression in young adults: associations with systemic inflammation and early life adversity.
papers.abstract: 1BackgroundThere is limited research on persistent or recurrent depression into young adulthood. We examined the prevalence of recurrent/persistent depression in young adults, and associations with childhood trauma/adversity and systemic inflammation, and if inflammatory markers mediated associations between childhood trauma and subsequent depression. MethodsALSPAC participants with ICD-10 depression assessments at ages 18, 24 and 30 were classified as never depressed, transiently depressed (one episode), or persistently/recurrently depressed ([≥]2 episodes). Trauma/adversity from birth to age 16/17 was characterised by type, timing and burden. Interleukin-6 (IL-6) and C-reactive protein (CRP) were measured at ages 9, 16, 18 and 24. Analyses used multinomial logistic regression, linear regression and causal mediation models. ResultsAmong 2,014 participants, 78.9% were never depressed, 15.0% had transient depression and 6.1% had persistent/recurrent depression. Trauma/adversity was more strongly associated with persistent/recurrent depression (RRR 3.17, 95% CI 1.98-5.06; FDR-P=6.2x10-) than transient depression, with a dose-response pattern and stronger associations for threat adversities. Middle-to-late childhood (11-17 yrs) emerged as a sensitive period for persistent/recurrent (RRR 2.85, 95% CI 1.47-5.52) and transient depression (RRR 1.85, 95% CI 1.25-2.73). Trauma/adversity was associated with modestly higher IL-6 at age 24 (all FDR-adjusted P<0.05); CRP associations did not survive multiple-testing correction. Neither marker mediated trauma/adversity associations with persistent/recurrent depression. ConclusionPersistent/recurrent depression affects approximately 1 in 20 young adults. Childhood trauma/adversity, particularly during middle-to-late childhood, was associated with persistent/recurrent depression, but measured inflammatory proteins did not mediate this association. Further work is needed to understand biological mechanisms underlying the embedding early life psychosocial stress.

papers.title: Functional connectivity of reward and cognitive control networks predicts body mass index but not binge eating disorder in women
papers.abstract: BackgroundBinge eating disorder (BED) is associated with obesity as well as behavioral and neurobiological changes in the reward and cognitive control systems of the brain. To better dissociate neural mechanisms of pathological eating behavior, functional connectivity (FC) analyses have shown promise. However, there is currently no replicable signature of BED derived from fMRI. MethodsWe investigated FC in 61 women with varying symptoms of binge eating. The three groups included 21 women with BED, 20 women with subsyndromal BED (subBED), and 20 controls without binge eating (noBE) matched in body mass index (BMI) and age. To identify neural signatures of BED and BMI, we used seed-based FC "fingerprints" (nucleus accumbens, NAcc, for reward and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, dlPFC, for cognitive control) to predict group or BMI based on resting state and task-based (food bidding) FC. Furthermore, we explored spatial patterns of FC to quantify associations with BED and BMI. ResultsBoth seeds of the reward and cognitive control networks robustly predicted BMI (rs = .33 - .46). The dlPFC seed predicted BMI across conditions (resting state: p=.002; task: p=.012) while the NAcc seed only predicted BMI based on task-based FC (p=.007). In contrast, FC failed to classify binge eating groups better than chance. ConclusionsFC within reward and cognitive control networks primarily reflect obesity-related changes. Despite pronounced differences in eating behavior, BED could not be reliably dissociated from subBED or noBE using FC fingerprints. These results highlight challenges in identifying BED-specific functional markers. papers.title: Menstrual Cycle Exacerbation of ADHD Symptoms in Adults: Common, Person-Specific, and Not Confined to the Luteal Phase
papers.abstract: ObjectivePatients often describe menstrual-cycle worsening of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). We prospectively evaluated sample- and person-level cycle effects on ADHD symptoms and their independence from cyclical negative affect and pain. MethodsIn an intensive longitudinal cohort (2019-2024), 106 naturally cycling adults meeting DSM-5 ADHD criteria on integrated assessment rated daily inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity (Barkley Adult ADHD Rating Scale-IV), negative affect, and pain (median, 41 days) and provided daily salivary estradiol and progesterone for ovulation coding and phase-aligned cycle time (PACTS). Generalized additive models estimated sample-level and person-specific cycle curves; robust cyclicity was tested against each participants own time-shuffle null. Lab cognitive testing at four counterbalanced phases provided post hoc validation. ResultsSample-average cycle effects were significant yet small (<1% of daily variance), but 54% of 87 participants tested individually were robustly cyclical in ADHD symptoms (95% CI, 44%-64%; inattention 43%, hyperactivity-impulsivity 26%), more often with informant-confirmed ADHD (69% vs 36%). Among them, the cycle explained median 52% and 51% of symptom variance, a mean swing of 2.6 and 2.1 DSM-5 criteria. Most remained cyclical after adjustment for affect (68%) or pain (81%). Worsening most often peaked at and after menses rather than premenstrually; no cycle met prospective criteria for premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD). Hormones did not differ by cyclicity. ConclusionsAbout half of these adults with ADHD showed robust cyclical symptom change, mostly not reducible to cyclical affect or pain and usually outside the premenstrual window. Future work should test its stability and whether a DSM-5 cyclical specifier is warranted.

papers.title: Cortical brain changes from early to mid-adolescence in offspring at familial high risk for schizophrenia or bipolar disorder
papers.abstract: Objective: Schizophrenia (SZ) and bipolar disorder (BP) emerge in late adolescence or adulthood. Offspring at familial high risk for SZ (FHR-SZ) or BP (FHR-BP) are more likely to develop psychiatric disorders. Prior work from the Danish High Risk and Resilience (VIA) Study found sex-specific volumetric brain differences in offspring at FHR-SZ and FHR-BP aged 11-12 years. This study builds upon these findings by testing whether they reflect group differences in rate of change or stable group differences from early to mid-adolescence. Methods: This study investigated MRI data from offspring at FHR-SZ, FHR-BP, and population- based controls (PBC) at baseline (11-12 years; n=288) and follow-up (15-16 years; n=249). FreeSurfer longitudinal processing derived total brain volume, cortical measures, and intracranial volume (ICV). Linear mixed-effects models tested group-by-age interactions and sex-specific group effects, as well as associations with psychotic experiences (PE) and lifetime Axis-I mental disorders. Results: The analysis did not detect group-by-age interactions, indicating similar developmental slopes across groups. However, at both time points, males at FHR-SZ demonstrated reduced brain and cortical volumes compared to PBC and FHR-BP males. These effects were attenuated after adjusting for ICV, which was reduced in males at FHR-SZ. The analysis additionally detected volumetric reductions in males with PE, after controlling for risk status. Conclusions: These results extend the previous findings to ages 15-16 years, indicating group differences are stable and persist into mid-adolescence. Associations with ICV suggest early neurodevelopmental effects, and volumetric reductions in males with PE suggest convergent effects with FHR-SZ.

papers.title: Association of Outpatient Crisis Services with Emergency Department Revisits in Suicidal Youth
papers.abstract: Background and ObjectivePediatric emergency department (ED) visits for suicidal ideation and behavior have increased substantially, highlighting the need for scalable outpatient interventions that reduce recurrent ED use. We tested whether referral to outpatient crisis services was associated with fewer mental health-related ED revisits, hypothesizing that referred youth would have lower revisit rates than those receiving usual community care. MethodsWe conducted a quasi-experimental study of 3,125 youth presenting with suicidal ideation or behavior to a large academic childrens health system between October 1, 2023, and August 31, 2025. Youth were referred to outpatient crisis services or community treatment (usual care) based on slot availability and clinician discretion. Propensity score modeling balanced demographic, clinical, and prior treatment characteristics between groups. ResultsAmong 3,125 qualifying index ED visits, 763 (24.4%) youth were referred to crisis services and 461 (14.8%) received [≥]1 crisis visit within 30 days. In intent-to-treat analyses, referral was associated with fewer mental health-related ED revisits at 90 days (adjusted incidence rate ratio [aIRR], 0.67; 95% CI, 0.56-0.81) and 180 days (aIRR, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.59- 0.80). Associations were strongest among youth requiring short-term hospitalization (aIRR, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.36-0.58) and those with moderate-to-high suicide risk (aIRR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.39- 0.61). Findings were consistent in as-treated analyses. ConclusionOutpatient crisis services were associated with substantially fewer mental health-related ED revisits among suicidal youth, with the largest reductions among youth with greater clinical acuity.

papers.title: Trends in Gambling-Related Primary Care Encounters in Brazil, 2014-2025
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of online gambling and sports betting has raised concerns about gambling-related harm and its implications for public health. However, nationwide evidence regarding temporal trends and patterns of health care utilization associated with gambling remains limited, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. We conducted a nationwide retrospective study using administrative data from Brazils Unified Health System from 2014 through 2025. We examined primary health care records associated with pathological gambling (ICD-10, code F63.0) and gambling and betting (code Z72.6). We analyzed temporal trends, seasonal patterns, and geographic and demographic distributions, calculating annual encounter rates per 100,000 inhabitants. Gambling-related primary health care encounters increased substantially during the study period, with a marked acceleration beginning in 2022. By 2025, nationwide rates reached 1.46 encounters per 100,000 inhabitants for pathological gambling and 0.60 per 100,000 for gambling and betting. Increases were observed across all five Brazilian regions, with the highest rates in the South and Southeast. Recorded encounters increased across age groups and both sexes, particularly among adults aged 20 to 39 years. Rates were also elevated among adolescent males and older women. Time-series analyses suggested seasonal variation, with higher indices generally between April and October. Gambling-related encounters in Brazilian primary health care increased markedly from 2014 through 2025, particularly after 2022, with substantial demographic and geographic variation. These findings indicate increasing documentation of gambling-related conditions within a nationwide public health system and underscore the need for improved surveillance, early identification, and access to appropriate mental health care.

papers.title: Secondary Analysis of Treatment Effect Heterogeneity of priovi in Borderline Personality Disorder
papers.abstract: The digital therapeutic priovi has small average effects for borderline personality disorder (BPD). In this preregistered secondary analysis, we aimed to explore the heterogeneity and potential moderators of these effects. Adults received priovi plus treatment as usual or treatment as usual alone. At the 3-month primary endpoint (N = 528), model-based recursive partitioning showed heterogeneous effects on Borderline Symptom List-23 (BSL-23) change (p = 0.022) and on clinically relevant response (p = 0.007). Benefit was larger at higher baseline symptom load: a representative tree split on Patient Health Questionnaire-9 at a score of 23, and the higher-score subgroup had roughly twice the BSL-23 reduction (conditional average treatment effects -0.40 versus -0.19). Baseline BSL-23, depressive symptoms, and recent life-threatening events ranked as the leading moderators. Quartile calibration of predicted CATEs was weak and non-monotonic. The moderators are hypothesis-generating and should not guide patient selection without external validation.

papers.title: Patterns of Childhood Exposomes, White Matter Development and Behaviors Link to Future Cognition and Psychopathology in Youth
papers.abstract: Environmental exposures during childhood strongly impact individuals cognitive and socioemotional development, and psychiatric vulnerability. However, childhood exposures rarely occur in isolation. Instead, they form a highly correlated exposome whose multidimensional relationships with brain development and behavioral outcomes remain poorly understood. Elucidating the complex interplay between brain, behavior, and environment requires a multivariate approach. This study used regularized multiset canonical correlation analysis on longitudinal data from 8,113 preadolescents in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study to characterize latent multivariate dimensions linking diverse environmental exposures, tract-wisely resolved measures of white matter (WM) development and integrity, and multi-domain behavioral phenotypes and relate them to concurrent and future psychopathology. Two distinct multivariate dimensions were identified exhibiting different exposure, WM development, and behavior patterns. The first linked greater socioeconomic resources to more advanced WM development, particularly in dorsal-association tracts, and superior cognitive performance. The second dimension linked stronger psychosocial support with higher WM integrity, more advanced development of limbic tracts, and lower levels of psychopathology. Longitudinal analyses revealed differential contributions of these dimensions to follow-up cognitive, socioemotional and psychiatric outcomes. Moreover, WM and exposomic variates in these dimensions moderated the effects of childhood adversity on transdiagnostic psychiatric disorder risk, in sex-and context-specific fashions. Together, these findings clarify how childhood environmental exposures and the linked WM developmental differences relate to cognition and psychopathology risk, potentially informing the identification of candidate neural targets for future interventions.

papers.title: The Antipsychotic Load (AP_Load2026): a normalised prescribed-dose index for schizophrenia research
papers.abstract: Background and HypothesisSchizophrenia research routinely reduces antipsychotic treatment to a single number, but the available summaries disagree. Chlorpromazine equivalents, the WHO Defined Daily Dose (DDD) and the percentage of the licensed maximum (%BNFmax) rank the same patient differently, most of all for clozapine, whose dose-concentration relationship varies several-fold with sex and smoking. We hypothesised that referencing clozapine dose to a target individualised for sex and smoking would track plasma clozapine better than dose-proportional measures. Study DesignIn the Antipsychotic Load (AP_Load2026), each daily dose is expressed as a percentage of a reference dose, summed without a cap. Clozapine is referenced to a target individualised for sex and cigarettes per day, under two published anchor schemes, and other antipsychotics to a dose reconciling the WHO DDD and the licensed maximum. The clozapine term was tested against plasma clozapine (1316 assessments, 255 patients) with log-log mixed-effects models, and the non-clozapine reference against independently derived published doses. Study ResultsThe individualised reference tracked plasma clozapine better than any dose-proportional measure (marginal R{superscript 2} 0.249 v. 0.166; {Delta}R{superscript 2} 0.082, 95% CI 0.044-0.120). The scheme with the larger smoking correction fitted better (0.249 v. 0.231), an ordering robust to quality-control variants and co-prescription. Of five candidate references for other antipsychotics, %BNFmax was the least consistent with external criteria. ConclusionsAP_Load2026 is a transparent framework for normalising prescribed antipsychotic dose. Its clozapine reference is validated against a biomarker, whereas the reference for other antipsychotics is a calibrated convention at least comparable with existing alternatives. The index is particularly suited to treatment-resistant and clozapine-enriched cohorts.

papers.title: Proteomic profiling of postmortem prefrontal cortex identifies molecular signatures of borderline personality disorder
papers.abstract: Borderline personality disorder (BPD) is characterized by a severe pattern of symptoms including emotional instability, impulsivity, and unstable interpersonal relationships. A complex interplay between genetics and environmental factors has been hypothesized to be associated with the development of BPD. While neuroimaging studies have identified structural and functional changes in the brain, and genome-wide association studies described some first genetic risk loci, the neurobiological underpinnings of BPD remain poorly described. To better understand disease processes in BPD, we performed a molecular characterization of the prefrontal cortex (PFC), an important brain region for emotion and impulsivity regulation in BPD. Label-free brain proteomics was performed in postmortem human brain tissue in a sample of n=79, with a case group of n=36 individuals with BPD and a control group of n=43 individuals without BPD. Differential protein expression analysis suggested protein-level dysregulation of mitochondrial, immunological, and neuroplasticity pathways. Network analyses identified a BPD-associated co-expression module enriched for protein secretory and synaptic processes that is druggable with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors. Additional druggability analyses on protein-protein interaction networks and drug-repositioning analysis suggested VEGF signaling as a potential pharmacologic target in BPD. When we integrated BPD proteomic signatures with genomic and proteomic datasets of common comorbidities such as posttraumatic stress disorder and major depressive disorder, we observed a strong convergent overlap across disorders, with STX7 and RTN4 identified as conserved, differentially expressed proteins. Our study provides first insights into proteomic signatures of BPD in the brain, suggests potential pharmacological targets, and provides evidence for convergent protein signatures across BPD and common comorbidites.

papers.title: Neurotransmitter-specific polygenic scores dissect clinical heterogeneity in schizophrenia
papers.abstract: Schizophrenia (SCZ) is a highly heritable psychiatric disorder characterised by substantial clinical heterogeneity. While global polygenic scores (gPGS) capture genetic liability to SCZ, their ability to explain clinical variability remains limited. Pathway-stratified polygenic scores (sPGS) offer a biologically informed approach to patient stratification. In this study, common genetic variants were annotated across five neurotransmitter (NT) signalling pathways -- acetylcholine (ACh), dopamine, {gamma}-aminobutyric acid (GABA), glutamate (Glu), and serotonin. sPGS adjusted for sex and ancestry principal components, were calculated in two independent cohorts with different available clinical data (N=3,044 and N=645). By clustering top-decile individuals across the five sPGS dimensions, we classified patients into five mutually exclusive patient profiles, which were then evaluated for their associations with Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) symptom dimensions, age at disease onset (AAO), and three-year clinical remission and treatment response. Although gPGS showed no significant association with clinical outcomes, some sPGS-derived profiles captured clinically relevant heterogeneity across cohorts. Patients assigned to the Ach profile exhibited higher overall symptom severity, particularly negative symptoms and general psychopathology. Patients within the Glu profile were characterised by more severe negative symptoms, earlier AAO, reduced three-year remission, and poorer treatment response. Similarly, the GABA risk profile was also associated with three-year remission rates. These findings suggest that NT pathway-specific polygenic profiling may capture clinically relevant variation overlooked by genome-wide approaches. By identifying genetic profiles associated with symptom severity, disease onset, and longitudinal outcomes, this framework could contribute to biologically informed patient stratification and inform future precision psychiatry approaches in SCZ.

papers.title: Effectiveness of AI-Supported Holistic Health Management Through PREVERY's Digital Health Promotion and Prevention Program: A Prospective Before-and-After Observational Study
papers.abstract: BackgroundThere is an increasing strain on our healthcare system due to rising numbers of diseases related to chronic stress. One approach to combat these stress-related complaints is health coaching. However, personal health coaching is expensive and time costly, while digital offers can complement the already existing health coaching strategies. Therefore, this study investigates the effects of an AI-supported, digital health and prevention program. Methods253 participants were included in the study, with 113 being analyzed eventually. General stress experience and self-efficacy were assessed at baseline (T1), after six weeks (T2), and three months after the interventional phase (T3) via a Numerical Analog Scale (NAS) with values ranging from 0 to 10, the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS), and the PsyCap Scale (CPC). ResultsA significant time effect was observed for CPC and PSS. CPC increased significantly from T1 to T2 and T3 and remained stable between T2 and T3, while PSS decreased from T1 to T2 and increased again by T3. All pairwise comparisons were significant. There were also significant time effects for self-reported current health status, health literacy, health awareness, and self-efficacy, with values at T3 being higher than at T1 (for health awareness, this was already evident at T2; for self-efficacy, this was additionally evident between T2 and T3), while no time effect was found for motivation. ConclusionPREVERY seems to be an effective prevention program to increase psychological capital together with self-reported current health status, health awareness, health literacy, and self-efficacy, while at the same time reducing perceived stress.

papers.title: A robust coordinated molecular response following trauma promotes recovery and protects against chronic pain and neuropsychiatric symptoms
papers.abstract: The biological mechanisms governing recovery versus chronicity of adverse posttraumatic neuropsychiatric sequelae (APNS) remain poorly understood. Here, we characterized longitudinal molecular changes among trauma survivors across ten APNS domains, including pain, anxiety, and depression. Recovery across these diverse clinical outcomes was associated with a shared, temporally coordinated transcriptional signature, characterized by early innate immune activation, subsequent homeostatic and wound-healing processes, and later adaptive immune responses. In contrast, chronic APNS trajectories exhibited limited transcriptional remodeling. We derived and externally validated an RNA-based Recovery Score (RRS) capturing the shared molecular response underlying recovery. Higher RRS was associated with greater clinical recovery, elevated peritraumatic cortisol, and lower cumulative stress exposure. Drug-response profiling identified candidate compounds predicted to mimic recovery-associated transcriptional changes. Together, these findings support posttraumatic recovery as an active biological process and identify shared molecular pathways that may be harnessed to prevent multiple adverse posttraumatic outcomes.

papers.title: SHARED GENETIC ARCHITECTURE AND DIRECTIONAL ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN ATTENTION-DEFICIT/HYPERACTIVITY AND BORDERLINE PERSONALITY DISORDERS: AN INTEGRATIVE GENOMIC ANALYSIS
papers.abstract: Background: attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and borderline personality disorder (BPD) frequently co-occur, but their shared genetic susceptibility and directional associations remain unclear. Methods: we analyzed European-ancestry genome-wide association study (GWAS) data for ADHD (38,691 cases; 186,843 controls) and BPD (12,339 cases; 1,041,717 controls). Linkage disequilibrium score regression, conjunctional false discovery rate (conjFDR), bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR), MR accounting for linkage disequilibrium and sample overlap (MR-LAP), Causal Analysis Using Summary Effect estimates (CAUSE), colocalization, and Sum of Single Effects (SuSiE) fine-mapping assessed genetic sharing and directionality. Results: genetic correlation was substantial (r_g = 0.733). ConjFDR identified 48 shared loci; 36 (75%) showed concordant directions in both phenotype-specific comparisons. Functional annotation implicated axon guidance, oxidative phosphorylation, and developing midbrain cells. ADHD-to-BPD MR was positive (22 instruments; inverse-variance weighted beta = 0.487, SE = 0.082, p = 3.27 x 10^-9), persisting after outlier removal, MR-LAP correction, and exclusion of two instruments at colocalized loci. Reverse MR was positive (five instruments; beta = 0.303, SE = 0.112, p = 6.83 x 10^-3) but heterogeneous and variant-sensitive. CAUSE favored directional over sharing-only models in both directions (delta ELPD = 6.98 and 5.92, respectively). SuSiE colocalization supported shared signals at rs17576773, rs9969232, and rs4727799. Conclusions: ADHD and BPD exhibit extensive genetic overlap involving 48 shared loci and convergent evidence of directional associations. Findings across complementary methods more consistently support an ADHD-to-BPD relationship, suggesting that shared genetic susceptibility alone may not fully explain their co-occurrence.
